facts.statement: Acanthorhachis is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish that lived during the Carboniferous period.
facts.quote: Acanthorhachis is an enigmatic extinct genus of chondrichthyan from the Carboniferous period.

facts.statement: The name Acanthorhachis comes from Greek words meaning "spine" and "backbone".
facts.quote: Its name is derived from the Greek word acanthos meaning "spine" and the Greek suffix for spine, -rhachis.

facts.statement: The animal's body was covered in spine-like dermal denticles and smaller subsidiary spines.
facts.quote: This is due to the spine-like dermal denticles and their subsidiary spines, which coated the exterior of the animal.

facts.statement: The type species was originally named Listracanthus spinatus by Herbert Bolton in 1896.
facts.quote: The type species Listracanthus spinatus was in 1896 named by Herbert Bolton.

facts.statement: The genus is currently monotypic, containing only the single species A. spinatus.
facts.quote: It is currently monotypic, containing only the species A. spinatus.

facts.statement: Fossils occur rarely in the Viséan-aged Eyam Limestone of Derbyshire, England.
facts.quote: It occurs rarely in Viséan-aged Eyam Limestone of Derbyshire, England.

facts.statement: The genus lived between 318.7 and 316.9 million years ago during the Bashkirian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Bashkirian to Bashkirian (318.7 to 316.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus belongs to the family Listracanthidae.
The animal is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
